4.x: V.D. Satheesan became Chief Minister of Kerala. Himanta Biswa Sarma is associated with Assam, Suvendu Adhikari with West Bengal and C. Joseph Vijay with Tamil Nadu.
4.tq: Start with the sure Chief Minister-State pair and eliminate swapped State associations.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: The United Democratic Front secured how many seats in the Kerala Assembly election of 9 April 2026?
4.x: The UDF won 102 of Kerala's 140 Assembly seats in the election held on 9 April 2026.
4.tq: Separate the alliance seat figure from the total strength of the Assembly.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Who was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Kerala on 18 May 2026?
4.x: Congress leader V.D. Satheesan was sworn in as Kerala Chief Minister on 18 May 2026, ending ten years of LDF rule.
4.tq: Use the date-office association to distinguish the Kerala result from other State changes.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s:
With reference to the Assam Assembly election held on 9 April 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Assembly has 126 seats.
2. The NDA won 102 seats.
3. The BJP won 82 seats.
4. Himanta Biswa Sarma began his second term as Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: All four statements are correct. Assam has 126 Assembly seats; the NDA won 102, including 82 for the BJP, and Himanta Biswa Sarma continued as Chief Minister for a second term.
4.tq: Verify the total, alliance share, party share and leadership outcome as separate components.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Which of the following was a major outcome of the West Bengal Assembly election of May 2026?
o: The NDA won 202 seats and Nitish Kumar continued as Chief Minister.
The BJP won 208 seats and Suvendu Adhikari became the first BJP Chief Minister of the State.
The UDF formed the government with 102 seats.
TVK formed the government under C. Joseph Vijay.
4.x: The BJP won 208 seats in West Bengal; Suvendu Adhikari became the State's first BJP Chief Minister and was sworn in on 9 May 2026.
4.tq: Link the party's landslide, the Chief Minister and the State without confusing neighbouring election results.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following statements about the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election is NOT correct?
o: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam formed the government.
Joseph Vijay became Chief Minister on 10 May 2026.
It produced the first non-DMK/AIADMK Chief Minister since 1956.
It ended approximately six decades of DMK-AIADMK duopoly.
4.x: The first non-DMK/AIADMK Chief Minister since 1967 was C. Joseph Vijay, not since 1956. The other three statements are correct.
4.tq: Find the altered year in the otherwise correct description of the Tamil Nadu result.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in as West Bengal Chief Minister.
B. C. Joseph Vijay was sworn in as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister.
C. V.D. Satheesan was sworn in as Kerala Chief Minister.
D. The Tamil Nadu trust vote was held.
4.x: The correct order is Suvendu Adhikari's oath on 9 May, C. Joseph Vijay's oath on 10 May, V.D. Satheesan's oath on 18 May, and the Tamil Nadu trust vote on 13 May is actually before 18 May; therefore the precise chronological order is A, B, D, C.
4.tq: Place the dated events first and check the middle events rather than relying only on election sequence.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: In the context of the Tamil Nadu Assembly election of May 2026, who became Chief Minister?
4.x: C. Joseph Vijay of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on 10 May 2026.
4.tq: Identify the correct leader-State combination among contemporaneous election outcomes.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Which of the following changes took place in Karnataka in June 2026?
o: Himanta Biswa Sarma replaced Siddaramaiah as Chief Minister.
Siddaramaiah replaced D.K. Shivakumar as Chief Minister.
Suvendu Adhikari replaced Siddaramaiah as Chief Minister.
D.K. Shivakumar replaced Siddaramaiah as Chief Minister.
4.x: D.K. Shivakumar replaced Siddaramaiah as the Chief Minister of Karnataka in June 2026.
4.tq: Use the office-change pattern and distinguish the outgoing and incoming Chief Minister.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Who was elected Vice-President of India in September 2025?
4.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President of India in September 2025.
4.tq: Distinguish the constitutional office-holder from State-level political leaders.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the electoral college for the election of the Vice-President of India?
o: Only elected members of the Lok Sabha
Elected members of the Rajya Sabha and nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of all State Assemblies
Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, without members of State Legislative Assemblies
4.x: The Vice-President is elected by the elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament. Members of State Legislative Assemblies do not form part of this electoral college.
4.tq: Ask who would perform the constitutional function and distinguish the Vice-Presidential college from the Presidential college.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nominated members of Parliament participate in the election of the Vice-President.
2. Members of Legislative Assemblies participate in the election of the Vice-President.
3. Elected members of both Houses of Parliament form part of the Vice-Presidential electoral college.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. State Legislative Assembly members do not participate in the election of the Vice-President.
4.tq: Test the constitutional distinction between Parliament-based and Assembly-based electoral colleges.
4.sec: Elections held - States, results  [APPSC]

4.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to:
4.x: The 131st Amendment Bill proposed increasing the Lok Sabha cap from 550 to 850 members.
4.tq: Retain the exact numerical change rather than confusing the proposed cap with the existing strength.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed to use which Census for fast-tracking women's reservation?
4.x: The Bill proposed to use the 2011 Census for the proposed expansion and implementation of women's reservation by 2029.
4.tq: Use the Census-year trap, where nearby decades are plausible distractors.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following correctly states the fate of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: It was withdrawn before being introduced in the Lok Sabha.
It was defeated in the Lok Sabha by 298 votes to 230 among 528 members voting.
It was passed unanimously by both Houses of Parliament.
It was returned by the President for reconsideration after being passed by the Lok Sabha.
4.x: The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha, where the vote was 298–230 among 528 members voting, and it fell short of the special majority required under Article 368.
4.tq: Combine the vote figures with the correct legislative stage and status.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 is also known as:
4.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment is known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023.
4.tq: Discriminate between the official popular name and descriptions of other constitutional proposals.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Under the 106th Constitutional Amendment, women's reservation in legislatures is to commence after:
o: A resolution of every State Legislative Assembly
4.x: The women's quota provided by Article 334A is tied to the completion of a Census and delimitation exercise; the material specifies Census 2027 and delimitation.
4.tq: Identify the stated precondition instead of treating the amendment as immediately operative.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Which Article was inserted by the 106th Constitutional Amendment to provide for women's reservation?
4.x: Article 334A was inserted to provide for women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, subject to the stated Census and delimitation conditions.
4.tq: Use the exact Article-number distinction among closely numbered constitutional provisions.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 proposed automatic removal from office of which persons after being held in custody for 30 consecutive days on serious charges?
o: Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts
The Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers
4.x: The Bill proposed the automatic removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers or Ministers if held in custody for 30 consecutive days for charges carrying a possible sentence of five years or more.
4.tq: Match the proposed power and its office-holders without expanding the provision to unrelated constitutional authorities.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: For the removal mechanism proposed in the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, the charges must carry a possible imprisonment of at least:
4.x: The proposed mechanism applied to charges carrying a sentence of five years or more, along with the 30-day custody condition.
4.tq: Separate the imprisonment threshold from the independent 30-day custody requirement.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 is correct?
o: It was defeated in the Lok Sabha by 298 votes to 230.
It was placed on the agenda of the July 2026 Monsoon Session and immediately enacted.
It amended Article 82A to introduce simultaneous elections.
It was left out of the July 2026 Monsoon Session agenda and was associated with a Joint Parliamentary Committee whose deadline was extended.
4.x: The Bill was left out of the July 2026 Monsoon Session agenda; it was before a Joint Parliamentary Committee and its deadline was extended. The other options describe the 131st or 129th proposals.
4.tq: Use the bill-number and status distinction to avoid swapping provisions among constitutional amendment proposals.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down which policy?
o: Bihar's 85% reservation in all Union Government jobs
Haryana's 75% reservation of private-sector jobs for local residents
A 50% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha
Assam's reservation for members of the Legislative Assembly
4.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down Haryana's policy reserving 75% of private-sector jobs for local residents.
4.tq: Identify the exact State, sector and percentage in a domicile-reservation dispute.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Which issue is associated with Bihar's proposed 85% reservation in 2025?
o: The electoral college for the Vice-President
The constitutional limit or ceiling of 50% on reservations
The number of Lok Sabha seats under Article 82A
4.x: Bihar's proposal for 85% reservation led to debate concerning the 50% reservation ceiling.
4.tq: Connect the numerical proposal with the constitutional issue it raises, rather than with unrelated reservation provisions.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 is significant because it is:
o: A Union law applicable only to Parliament
The second UCC Bill in the North-East and the fifth at the State level
The first UCC Bill in India and the first in the North-East
The first UCC Bill in the North-East and the third at the State level in India
4.x: The Assam UCC Bill, 2026 was described as the first such Bill in the North-East and the third State-level UCC Bill overall.
4.tq: Compare the regional and national ranking separately to avoid reversing first and third.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding constitutional amendment proposals:
List-I (Bill/Amendment)
a. 129th Amendment Bill, 2024
a. 130th Amendment Bill, 2025
c. 131st Amendment Bill, 2026
d. 106th Amendment, 2023

List-II (Provision/subject)
i. Women's reservation linked to Census and delimitation
ii. One Nation One Election
iii. Removal of certain Ministers after 30 days in custody
iii. Expansion of Lok Sabha cap and women's reservation by 2029

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
4.x: The 129th Bill concerned One Nation One Election; the 130th concerned removal after prolonged custody; the 131st proposed expansion of the Lok Sabha and women's reservation; and the 106th provided women's reservation linked to Census and delimitation. In the options, the repeated labels in List-II represent the third and fourth entries respectively.
4.tq: Start from the distinctive bill numbers and match each with its unique subject.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: The 129th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2024 proposed the insertion of which Article in connection with One Nation One Election?
4.x: The 129th Amendment Bill proposed a new Article 82A and amendments to Articles 83 and 172 in relation to simultaneous elections.
4.tq: Match the amendment proposal with its exact constitutional Article rather than its broader political slogan.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s: Which Articles, besides the proposed Article 82A, were identified for amendment by the 129th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2024?
4.x: The 129th Amendment Bill proposed a new Article 82A and amendments to Articles 83 and 172 for One Nation One Election.
4.tq: Test the precise constitutional provisions instead of accepting a broad description of simultaneous elections.
4.sec: Reservation and constitutional amendments  [APPSC]

4.s:
The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, provides for the establishment of the National Tribunals Commission. Which one of the following is correct regarding its composition and tenure?
1. Its headquarters will be at New Delhi.
2. It will consist of five members.
3. The tenure will be five years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: The National Tribunals Commission under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, has its headquarters at New Delhi, consists of five members and provides a five-year or 70-year age limit for tenure.
4.tq: Use the statement-combination method and verify each institutional detail separately.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, was introduced primarily to replace which of the following?
4.x: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, replaces the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.
4.tq: Identify the replacing legislation rather than the institutional body created by it.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026:
1. It changes the name of Kerala to Keralam.
2. The change was approved by the Lok Sabha on 11 August 2026 and by the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.
3. The name of the High Court is also changed by the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: The Act changes Kerala to Keralam, with Lok Sabha approval on 11 August and Rajya Sabha approval on 12 August 2026. The High Court name remains unchanged.
4.tq: Find the false statement by checking the exception relating to the High Court.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, operates through an alteration in which constitutional provision and Schedule?
4.x: The change from Kerala to Keralam is made under Article 3 and involves the First Schedule of the Constitution.
4.tq: Apply the article-and-Schedule pairing technique used for constitutional amendments.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment, 2026, provides for which of the following penalties for specified offences?
o: Two to five years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹10 lakh
Life imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh
Five to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹1 crore
Five to ten years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh
4.x: The amendment provides for imprisonment of five to ten years and a fine of up to ₹50 lakh.
4.tq: Distinguish the exact punishment range and monetary ceiling.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: Under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment, 2026, investigation of an unfair-means case is to be completed within:
4.x: The amendment requires the probe to be completed within 60 days and provides for special fast-track courts.
4.tq: Use the precise statutory time-limit as the distinguishing fact.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025?
o: It replaces MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 and provides 125 days of employment with a base wage of ₹300 per day.
It replaces MGNREGA from 1 January 2026 and provides 100 days of employment with a base wage of ₹250 per day.
It supplements MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 and provides 150 days of employment with a base wage of ₹300 per day.
It replaces the National Food Security Act from 1 July 2026 and provides 125 days of employment.
4.x: The VB-G RAM G Act replaces MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, provides 125 days of employment and fixes a base wage of ₹300 per day.
4.tq: Separate the effective date, employment guarantee and wage figure before selecting the complete option.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, is associated with which of the following provisions?
o: Regulation of only educational online games
A ban on real-money games and establishment of an Online Gaming Authority of India under the 2026 Rules
Transfer of online gaming regulation exclusively to State Governments
A ban on all forms of online games, including recreational games
4.x: The Act bans real-money games, while the 2026 Rules establish the Online Gaming Authority of India from 1 May 2026.
4.tq: Distinguish a targeted prohibition from an exaggerated ban on every online game.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025, replaced which of the following laws?
o: Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
Atomic Energy Act, 1948 and Nuclear Safety Act, 2010
Electricity Act, 2003 and Atomic Energy Act, 1962
Environment Protection Act, 1986 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
4.x: The SHANTI Act, 2025, replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.
4.tq: Start from the sure pair of Acts replaced by the new legislation.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the SHANTI Act, 2025?
o: A limited role for private entities
Unlimited supplier liability for nuclear damage
A liability cap of 300 million SDR
4.x: The SHANTI Act provides for no supplier liability, a limited private role and a cap of 300 million SDR; it does not impose unlimited supplier liability.
4.tq: Find the option that reverses the central liability provision.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026, increased the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to:
4.x: The amendment increases the Supreme Court strength from 34 to 38, comprising 37 judges apart from the Chief Justice of India.
4.tq: Distinguish the total strength from the number of judges excluding the CJI.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026, amended which legislation?
o: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956
4.x: The 2026 amendment amended the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, in connection with Article 124.
4.tq: Match the amendment with the parent statute rather than the constitutional article alone.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment), 2026, makes insulting or disrupting which of the following punishable?
4.x: The amendment to the 1971 Act makes insulting or disrupting Vande Mataram punishable.
4.tq: Use the exact protected national symbol instead of substituting a more familiar one.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, is primarily concerned with which subject and ministry?
o: Critical minerals fiscal regime — Ministry of Mines
Coal mine rehabilitation — Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Rare earth research — Ministry of Science and Technology
4.x: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, establishes a fiscal regime for critical minerals and is associated with the Ministry of Mines.
4.tq: Match the legislative subject with the responsible ministry.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following amendments removes self-determination of gender?
4.x: The Transgender Persons (Amendment), 2026, removes self-determination of gender; the amendment was made in March 2026.
4.tq: Apply the provision to the legislation most directly connected with the subject.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, provides that which of the following shall be the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh?
4.x: The Act declares Amaravati to be the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh, retrospectively from 2 June 2024.
4.tq: Identify the location and separately note the retrospective effective date.
4.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

4.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the adjudicating authority for insolvency resolution is the:
o: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
4.x: The National Company Law Tribunal is the adjudicating authority under the IBC. Appeals lie to the NCLAT, and resolution is intended to occur within 180 to 330 days.
4.tq: Distinguish the original adjudicating body from the appellate body.
4.sec: Acts in news - provisions, amending Acts  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relationship between the NCLT and NCLAT under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
o: NCLAT is the adjudicating authority and NCLT is the appellate forum.
NCLAT functions as the appellate forum against orders of NCLT.
Both bodies function only as advisory bodies.
4.x: The NCLT acts as the adjudicating authority, while appeals against its orders lie before the NCLAT.
4.tq: Discriminate between the adjudicating and appellate authorities.
4.sec: Acts in news - provisions, amending Acts  [APPSC]

4.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fast-track courts in India:
1. There are 884 fast-track courts in 21 States and Union Territories.
2. These courts have 17.54 lakh pending cases.
3. They function only in matters relating to taxation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: There are 884 fast-track courts in 21 States and Union Territories with 17.54 lakh pending cases. Their jurisdiction is not limited only to taxation matters.
4.tq: Reject the overbroad subject restriction and retain the reported numerical facts.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is implemented through the collaboration of which two institutions?
o: Supreme Court e-Committee and National Informatics Centre
Law Commission and Election Commission of India
NITI Aayog and National Human Rights Commission
Department of Justice and Finance Commission
4.x: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is a joint initiative of the Supreme Court e-Committee and the National Informatics Centre.
4.tq: Match the digital justice project with its institutional partners.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: How many virtual courts for petty offences are associated with the e-Courts Mission Mode Project?
4.x: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project includes 30 virtual courts dealing with petty offences.
4.tq: Test the exact count instead of the broader concept of virtual courts.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: The Supreme Court functions fully in virtual mode on which of the following days?
4.x: The Supreme Court is fully virtual on Mondays and Fridays.
4.tq: Use the weekday pair as the precise distinguishing detail.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. One Case One Data — Supreme Court initiative
2. Su Sahayak — launched by the Supreme Court
3. Draft rules on AI in judiciary — June 2026
4. Four new Division Benches — July 2026
4.x: All four statements are correct. The Supreme Court launched One Case One Data and Su Sahayak in May 2026, issued draft AI rules in June 2026 and added four Division Benches in July 2026.
4.tq: Confirm each date-and-initiative pair before choosing the complete combination.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: According to the India Justice Report 2025, which one of the following correctly represents the judicial infrastructure indicators?
o: About 15 judges per million people, fewer than 2,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 25 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 3.5 crore pending cases
About 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 10 judges per million people, more than 7,600 vacancies and over 4.5 crore pending cases
4.x: The India Justice Report 2025 records approximately 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases.
4.tq: Compare all three numerical indicators as a single data set.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Collegium system is correct?
o: It is expressly provided in the Constitution and was established in 1950.
It was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment and replaced by the NJAC in 2015.
It was established through an Act of Parliament in 1998.
It is not expressly mentioned in the Constitution and emerged through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 judgment.
4.x: The Collegium system is not expressly provided in the Constitution; it evolved through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 decision. The NJAC created by the 99th Amendment was struck down in 2015.
4.tq: Separate constitutional text from judicially evolved practice.
4.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

4.s: The renaming of Jonnagiri Gold Mine in Andhra Pradesh as Swarnagiri Gold Mine was undertaken in:
4.x: Jonnagiri Gold Mine was renamed Swarnagiri Gold Mine in July 2026 by the CDCA.
4.tq: Match the renaming event with its exact month and year.
4.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

4.s: Nauru was renamed in August 2026 as:
4.x: Nauru was renamed the Republic of Naoero in August 2026.
4.tq: Test the exact official form of the renamed country.
4.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

4.s: The Scheme for Promotion of International Cultural Relations was renamed as:
4.x: The Scheme for Promotion of International Cultural Relations was renamed the Global Engagement Scheme and is associated with the Ministry of Culture.
4.tq: Match the old scheme title with its new official name and ministry context.
4.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

4.s: How many districts does Andhra Pradesh have since December 2025?
4.x: Andhra Pradesh has 28 districts since December 2025; it had 26 districts from April 2022.
4.tq: Distinguish the latest figure from the earlier administrative count.
4.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

4.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, was promulgated under which Article of the Constitution?
4.x: The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under Article 123 in May 2026. Article 124 relates to the Supreme Court itself and its judges.
4.tq: Distinguish the ordinance-making Article from the substantive constitutional provision.
4.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

4.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, was replaced by a Bill passed by the Lok Sabha on:
4.x: The replacement Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 3 August 2026.
4.tq: Use the exact legislative date to connect the Ordinance with its replacement Bill.
4.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

4.s: Which Bill replaced the Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026?
4.x: The Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, was replaced by the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
4.tq: Identify the replacement Bill by matching its title with the Ordinance subject.
4.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

4.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance — June 2026
2. Sri City University Ordinance — Article 213
3. Supreme Court Number of Judges Ordinance — Article 213
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: The AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance was promulgated in June 2026, and the Sri City University Ordinance was issued under Article 213. The Supreme Court Ordinance was promulgated under Article 123, not Article 213.
4.tq: Use the constitutional division between Union and State ordinance powers to detect the swapped Article.
4.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

4.s: Which platform has been described as a one-stop Election Commission of India platform for draft electoral rolls and related services?
4.x: The ECINET app is intended to function as a one-stop ECI platform providing access to draft electoral rolls and other services.
